source: Mansfield et al. (2020), ApJL 888, L15, 'Evidence for H2 Dissociation and Recombination Heat Transport in the Atmosphere of KELT-9b' (doi:10.3847/2041-8213/ab5b09; arXiv:1910.01567v2). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve, program 14059, two AORs from BJD 2458414.2 to 2458416.3. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: equation 1 and Table 1 (tab:params).

model.equation: F_p = A1 cos[2 pi (t - t1)/p] + A2 cos[4 pi (t - t2)/p] (equation 1). The paper does not print the constant term; the planet's flux at mid-eclipse is taken to be the eclipse depth, which reproduces the paper's amplitude, hottest-hemisphere and nightside temperatures (see the report).

daysideK.where: Table 1, Dayside Brightness Temperature (PHOENIX stellar model)

notStated: The stellar brightness temperature used for the day and night temperatures (section 3 says PHOENIX models; section 5 uses 8287 K at 4.5 um for Teff 10200 K in the energy-balance model, which would give a 4739 K day side from this eclipse depth).
